items.title: Overview
items.text:
Welcome to Klipspringer. Klipspringer is an event ticketing and management platform. It's really good at handling very complex events and venues.

A (non-exhaustive) list of what Klipspringer offers:

  • mobile wallet support (Google Wallet and Samsung Wallet)
  • add-ons
  • schedules (and rsvps)
  • push notifications
  • roomsharing
  • single sign on (ldap, oidc, and saml)
  • memberships
  • waitlists
  • vouchers
  • promo codes
  • tax collection
  • ticket transfers
  • tiered tickets
  • sales reports
  • seat maps (reserved seating)
  • self-service kiosks
  • printing
  • point of sales
  • currency conversion.

Klipspringer is currently in beta so there is not much documentation yet.

items.title: Pricing
items.text:
Warning

Klipspringer is currently free during the beta. The following does not apply until the end of the beta. Pricing may change before the beta ends.

Klipspringer will charge 3% of the net price of the ticket, add-on, or membership. That's it.

items.title: Free tickets
items.text: Free tickets are free. We don't charge for those.

items.title: How is the fee calculated?
items.text:
It is 3% of the price of the product, excluding taxes. Examples:

  • If you charge $100 for a ticket, you will pay us $3.
  • If you charge $100 for a ticket and add 6% tax for a total of $106, you will still pay us $3.
  • If you charge $0 for a ticket, you will pay us $0.

items.title: What if I refund somebody?
items.text: We will credit the fee back on the next invoice if you do so through the software.

items.title: Does the fee apply to cash transactions or manual transfers?
items.text: Yes, if it was done through Klipspringer.

items.title: When are invoices issued?
items.text: The first day of the month at or around midnight (UTC). They're due 31 days later. There is interest of 1% (monthly) for overdue payments.

items.title: Does this include payment processor fees?
items.text: Payment processor fees are not included.

items.title: Is there special pricing for non-profits and small organizations?
items.text: Yes! Please contact us. We're always happy to work something out.

items.title: Kiosks
items.text:
Warning

This article is a stub. It will be updated as more information comes out.

A kiosk is a device where attendees can buy and print tickets without needing a cashier. A kiosk runs in a web browser or in the Klipspringer app. To set one up, go to the "Kiosks" tab in your event to start.

items.title: Security
items.text:
Each kiosk device is configured with its own PIN. To leave the kiosk, hold the top-left corner of the screen for 3 seconds, then enter the PIN. You may also unlock a device from the dashboard should you forget the PIN.

You should also lock it using your device's settings to prevent people from exiting the app easily.

items.title: iOS and iPadOS (recommended)
items.text:
1. Open your Settings app and go to Accessibility → Guided Access.
  2. Turn on "Guided Access"
  3. Set passcode for Guided Access.
  4. Open the Klipspringer app
  5. Click the home or side button three times
  6. Click "Start" on Guided Access

items.title: Android
items.text: The app will ask you if you wish to set the kiosk as the home screen. This is optional.

items.title: macOS, Windows, and Linux
items.text: You should consult your operating system's manual on kiosk support.

items.title: Items for sale
items.text: Choose the tickets and add-ons the kiosk sells from the "What attendees can buy" section in Kiosks. Products that need staff approval cannot be sold in the kiosk.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text:
Accessibility is a key feature of the Kiosk and does not require TalkBack or VoiceOver, as it is built into the application. It has support for high contrast, an audio guide, inverted colors, larger text, magnification, and can enable extra time for checkouts. These settings will reset when the next person starts their transaction

To enable the audio guide, you can touch and hold the screen for 2 seconds to turn it on.

items.title: Audio guide
items.text:
Dragging a finger across the screen will allow you to hear the item under your finger. Double tapping anywhere will allow you to choose the last item you heard. Swiping left or right will allow you to move between items.

When the audio guide is on, the seat picker will open in list view.

items.title: Notifications
items.text:
Warning

Don't use notifications for marketing. Many regions regulate unsolicited marketing by push notification, and attendees generally only agree to messages about events they signed up for.

Notifications are short messages to attendees before and during an event. Open Notifications in your event to write and send one. Team members need the "Send notifications" permission.

Use them for practical updates. For example, a conference might send "Check-in opens at the Congress center ar 11 AM. Please bring photo identification with you."

items.title: Delivery
items.text: Klipspringer delivers notifications through Google Wallet, or through the browser (if the attendee subscribed). Attendees who did neither won't receive them. You should share critical information in other ways too.

items.title: Payments
items.text: To sell paid products, connect a payment provider in your organization settings. Attendees pay by card or wallet through Stripe, or by manual payment such as a bank transfer. You can offer one or both. Free tickets need no payment provider.

items.title: Stripe
items.text: Open Settings in your organization and choose "Connect Stripe". Stripe asks for details about your business, such as its government identifier and who owns it.

items.title: In-person payments
items.text:
Klipspringer supports Stripe Terminal for payments at the box office and on kiosks. You'll need to purchase a card reader from Stripe directly.

Smart readers, such as the S700 and WisePOS E, connect over the internet. To add one, open the Klipspringer app, go to Account, then Card readers, and enter the code the reader shows. Bluetooth readers will connect through the Klipspringer app.

On a phone that supports Tap to Pay, the Klipspringer app can take payments without needing a dedicated reader.

items.title: Currency conversion
items.text:
Warning

Klipspringer isn't liable for incorrect conversion rates or for changes in rates.

With currency conversion on, attendees pay in their local currency at a rate from Stripe. Klipspringer locks the rate for 1 hour during checkout. You choose whether you pay the conversion fee or the attendee does.

items.title: Refunds
items.text: You can refund single items from a Stripe payment. The money returns to the attendee's original payment method.

items.title: Manual payment
items.text: Manual payment is for manual payments, such as bank transfers, money orders, and checks. Klipspringer wil give the attendee a reference number to include with their payment. When you get the payment, you'll need to go back and mark it as paid.

items.title: Refunds
items.text: You can refund single items from a manual payment, but Klipspringer can't send the money because it is a manual payment. You will need to refund the money yourself, and then mark it as refunded in the dashboard.

items.title: Products
items.text:
Klipspringer sells three kinds of products.

In simple terms:

  • a ticket admits its holder to the event
  • an add-on is an extra that people buy with a ticket
  • a membership gives discounts and access to events across your organization.

items.title: Ticket tiers
items.text:
Every ticket must belong to a tier. If you offer free admission, you will still need to make it a tier, but you can set the price to 0.

You can use tiers for each kind of admission you offer. For example, a conference might have a Guest tier for general admission, a Sponsor tier that includes the sponsors' dinner, and a Student tier limited to people 25 and under.

items.title: Add-ons
items.text: Addons can be restricted to a specific ticket, requiring any ticket, or not requiring anything. For example, you may have a dinner add-on that requires a Sponsor ticket.

items.title: Memberships
items.text:
A membership plan gives members free or discounted admission, guest passes, or access to member-only items.

For example, a museum might sell a 1-year membership for $80 that includes free daily admission, 10% off add-ons, and 2 guests per visit. Members must buy the plan again when it ends.

items.title: Questions at checkout
items.text: You can use custom questions to collect information you need to run the event, such as asking for allergies or T-shirt sizes. It is very important to only collect the information that you need, since it can cross into sensitive information.

items.title: Room sharing
items.text: Room sharing groups attendees who share lodging. Attendees can form groups with a code or you can match attendees who have no group. This may be useful if your event has shared lodging spaces (e.g., a camp or a group trip).

items.title: Rules
items.text:
There are some rules you can set in regards to room sharing.

Rule Description Minimum and maximum people The minimum and maximum group size. The maximum can be 2 to 12 people. Approval Who can approve a new group. Lock changes at The date and time after which attendees can't change their groups. Same ticket tier Everyone in a group in a group is paired by ticket tier Same gender Everyone in a group is paired by gender, which is declared using a custom question at checkout.

items.title: Managing groups
items.text: The Groups tab lists every group with its members and allows you to manage those groups. To download a CSV of all groups, choose "Export rooming list".

items.title: Schedules
items.text: The schedule lists the sessions at your event. Attendees will see it on the event page and can add sessions to their calendar. This is good if you host lightning talks, schedule dinners, or check-ins.

items.title: Sessions
items.text:
For each session, you can set a title, description, location, speaker, start time, and end time. You'll do this in the event's time zone.

Each session can be configured to be visible to different people. For example, a Sponsors' reception could be visible to your staff and sponsors, but would ultimately not be visible to the public.

items.title: RSVPs
items.text: Turn on "Accept RSVPs" on a session to let attendees tell you they plan to attend. The session's RSVP list shows who responded, and you can send those attendees a notification about things relating to that session.

items.title: Importing
items.text: If you have an existing calendar, you can import it to the Schedule using its ICS file.Klipspringer hides imported sessions until you edit each one and choose who can see it.

items.title: Allowing speakers to schedule sessions
items.text: If you invite speakers as an organizer and give them the "Create and delete their own schedule items" permission, they can create and manage their own sessions, but not other sessions.

items.title: Single sign-on
items.text:
Single sign-on allows people log in to Klipspringer through the identity provider they already use. Klipspringer supports Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0, Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), and OpenID Connect.

You'll need the "Manage single sign-on and verified domains" permission.

items.title: Connecting a provider
items.text:
1. Choose the provider type and enter a name. This is the name people will see on the login button
  2. Copy the details Klipspringer shows into your identity provider's settings.
  3. Test the connection. The test logs you in and shows the details your provider sends.

A provider can't be used until a test succeeds. If you change a connection setting, Klipspringer turns the provider off until you test it again.

You can connect unlimited providers.

items.title: Verified domains
items.text:
Klipspringer allows you to let organizers sign in with their identity provider only when you have verified the domain of their email address. To verify a domain, add the TXT record that Klipspringer gives you in your domain's DNS settings. Please note that a domain can only belong to one organization at a time.

Attendees logins do not require domain verification.

items.title: Access rules
items.text:
An access rule limits a product to people who match the rule. For example, a university can choose to sell student tickets only to people whose email address ends with "@university.edu".

Klipspringer checks the rule when an attendee adds the item to the cart and again at checkout.

items.title: Restrictions
items.text: Klipspringer doesn't let you disable or remove your last provider while single sign-on is required.

items.title: Sales tax and VAT
items.text:
Tax rules tell Klipspringer how much tax to charge. At checkout, Klipspringer selects the rule that matches the attendee's location and adds the tax to the order.

Warning

Klipspringer helps you collect and report tax. Nothing in this documentation constitutes legal or accounting advice. You are always responsible for how you collect and remit taxes.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Setting What it does Name A label which describes what the tax is for (e.g., "Sales Tax") Rate type A percentage or a fixed amount. Basis "Net" adds the tax on top of the price, while "Gross" means the price already includes the tax, so it won't update the total. Applies to Changes who the tax is applied to, which can be everyone, just EU countries, or just one country. Priority When several rules match, the rule with the highest priority applies.

For example, to add 8% sales tax on top of every ticket price, create a percentage rule at 8% with a Net basis that applies to everyone.

items.title: Calculation
items.text: Klipspringer subtracts all discounts and promotional codes first, then calculates tax on the rest of the total. Checkout will show the tax before the attendee pays. When the order completes, Klipspringer saves the tax rate on top of it. Changing the rule later won't affect existing orders.

items.title: Tickets
items.text: A ticket admits one attendee. Most tickets belong to a ticket tier, but members can also get in with a membership. Klipspringer issues tickets as PDFs, as Google Wallet passes, and on NFC cards.

items.title: Ticket page
items.text: Each attendee has a ticket page on your event site. From there, they can print out their PDF ticket or add it to their mobile wallet.

items.title: PDF tickets
items.text: Attendees can print a PDF ticket before they arrive. You can design the layout in the built-in drag-and-drop editor, with your own images, text, and variables. Examples of variables include attendee's name or ticket tier.

items.title: Google Wallet
items.text:
Klipspringer issues Google Wallet passes. To change the promoter name, hero image, or colors, open Settings in your event and choose Branding.

Each pass shows a QR code for your staff to scan. Klipspringer also sends notifications through Google Wallet. Read Notifications for more details.

Google Wallet passes also support Smart Tap. This means, your attendees can tap their card on your reader, similar to how tap to pay works. However, you'll need to obtain a certified reader through us. You'll need Klipspringer helper.

items.title: Samsung Wallet
items.text:
Klipspringer also issues Samsung Wallet passes. To change the hero image or colors, open Settings in your event and choose Branding.

Each pass shows a QR code for your staff to scan.

items.title: Apple Wallet
items.text: Apple Wallet isn't available yet.

items.title: NFC cards
items.text:
Klipspringer supports MIFARE DESFire® EV2, MIFARE DESFire® EV3, and MIFARE Ultralight® AES cards. DESFire is more secure and costs more. For example, a one-day festival that hands out thousands of wristbands might choose Ultralight AES, and a venue issuing year-long memberships might choose DESFire.

Each card holds keys unique to it, so a copied card doesn't work. Staff assign a card to an attendee at the point of sale in the Klipspringer app. Klipspringer avoids permanent changes to a card. Reading and assigning cards requires the app.

items.title: Transfers
items.text:
If you allow it, attendees can send a ticket to someone else.

QR Code is a registered trademark of DENSO WAVE INCORPORATED. MIFARE, MIFARE DESFire, and MIFARE Ultralight are registered trademarks of NXP B.V.

items.title: Venues
items.text: A venue is a place with regular opening hours, such as a museum or an attraction. Visitors choose a date, and sometimes a time, instead of attending a single event. To set one up, choose "Venue" when you create an event.

items.title: Entry types
items.text:
Each ticket tier has an entry type.

Entry type Valid for Single day Opening to closing on one date the visitor chooses. Multiple days A set number of consecutive days. Timed entry One arrival slot.

For example, a museum might sell a Single day general admission ticket, plus a Timed entry ticket for a special exhibit that admits 30 people every half hour.

items.title: Vouchers
items.text:
Warning

This article is a stub. It will be updated as more information comes out.

A voucher is a single-use code for one ticket or one add-on. As an example, you may give each speaker at your conference a voucher for a free ticket, or give your promoter 20 free tickets to hand out at will.

If a sign-in access rule restricts the covered item, the voucher will unlock it for the person who entered the code.

items.title: Waitlists
items.text:
A waitlist allows people to queue for a sold-out ticket. When tickets become available, Klipspringer offers them to people in the order that they joined. You can turn on a waitlist in the ticket tier settings. You cannot use a waitlist for seated tickets or for venues.

You can configure how long a waitlist offer lasts before it goes to the next person. By default, waitlist offers will last 24 hours. You should consider using shorter hold closer to the event so unclaimed tickets move on quicker.

items.title: GDPR
items.text:
Warning

This is not legal advice. We provide this documentation for general guidance but disclaim all liability from the use of this documentation.

items.title: Location
items.text: Klipspringer processes attendee data in the United States.

items.title: Cookies
items.text:
Klipspringer only uses a single cookie, kl_sid, which is used to maintain an active session, keep users logged in, and to store the user's shopping cart. Such cookies are classified as strictly necessary cookies within the meaning of Article 5(3) of Directive 2002/58/EC, and therefore do not require the display of a consent banner.

Your payment provider may add additional cookies. Stripe does this, for example.

items.title: Data controller
items.text: For the purposes of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you, as the event organiser, act as the Data Controller, determining the means and purposes of processing personal data. Klipspringer acts as your Data Processor, processing personal data solely on your behalf and in accordance with your documented instructions.

items.title: Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR)
items.text: Klipspringer has attendee data across various features. The "Personal data report" feature allows you to generate a PDF file of all of the personal information for an attendee. It may be accessed by visiting Organizational Dashboard → Attendees → [Attendee Name] → Download PDF Report.

items.title: Removal or correction of data
items.text:
You can modify the data of attendees from the dashboard. Klipspringer also allows the attendee to edit their data if the profile is not locked.

When an event is over, Klipspringer will allow you to scrub all personal information relating to an event. You can also anonymize or delete a specific attendee, although it won't remove their orders.

items.title: Klipspringer Organizer Privacy Policy
items.text: Effective date: 23 October 2026

items.title: 1. Who we are
items.text:
This Privacy Policy explains how Axostichus LLC ("Klipspringer," "we," "us") collects, uses, and shares personal information when you use Klipspringer.net and our services (the "Services").

Axostichus LLC 8735 Dunwoody Pl Ste R Atlanta, GA 30350 United States

privacy@klipspringer.net

items.title: 2. Two kinds of data, two roles
items.text:
We handle two kinds of personal information, and our role is different for each.

Organizer data. This is information about the businesses that use the Services and the people who work with them. It includes account holders, team members, and billing contacts. For this data, we decide how and why it is used. In legal terms, we are the "controller" or "business." This Policy covers organizer data.

Attendee data. This is information about people who buy, register for, or receive tickets and other items from organizers. The organizer decides how and why this data is used. We process it only on the organizer's instructions, to provide the Services. 

If you are an attendee, the organizer's privacy policy applies to your data. Please send any requests to the organizer. If you send a request to us, we will forward it to the organizer.

items.title: 3. What we collect about organizers
items.text:
Information you give us:

  • Account information: your name, work email, organization name, and password. We store passwords only as cryptographic hashes.
  • Team information: the names and work emails of team members you invite.
  • Billing information: your billing contact, billing address, and tax or VAT number. If you pay an invoice by card, our payment provider collects your card details. We do not see or store full card numbers.
  • Communications: support requests, complaints, and emails you send us.

Information we collect automatically:

  • Usage and device data: IP address, browser type, pages viewed, and timestamps. We collect this through server logs and essential cookies.

Information from others:

  • Your Payment Processor: whether your account is connected, and the fees we deducted.
  • Single sign-on providers: your identifier and basic profile details, if you sign in that way.
  • Your colleagues: your name and work email, if a team member invites you.

We need your account and billing information to provide the Services. Without it, we cannot open or run your account.

items.title: 4. How we use organizer data, and our legal bases
items.text:
The law in the EU, UK, and Switzerland requires a legal basis for each use of personal information. The table lists ours.

What we do Our legal basis Provide, operate, and support the Services Performing our contract with you Bill you and administer your account Performing our contract with you. For tax and accounting records, complying with a legal obligation. Send service messages, such as security alerts and changes to our Terms Performing our contract with you Keep the Services secure and prevent fraud and abuse Our legitimate interest in protecting the Services, our users, and attendees Review reports about content and handle complaints Complying with a legal obligation, and our legitimate interest in enforcing our Terms Improve and develop the Services Our legitimate interest in making the Services better. Where we can, we use de-identified or aggregated data. Comply with the law and respond to lawful requests Complying with a legal obligation. Where the obligation comes from a law outside the EU or UK, our legitimate interest in complying with it. Handle a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets Our legitimate interest in running and transferring our business

Where we rely on legitimate interests, we have weighed them against your rights. You may object at any time (see section 11).

items.title: 5. Automated decisions
items.text: We may use automated tools to help detect fraud, abuse, and security threats. A person reviews the case before we suspend or terminate an account. We do not make decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects on you based only on automated processing.

items.title: 6. How we share organizer data
items.text:
We share organizer data only with:

  • service providers who help us run the Services, such as hosting and email delivery providers. Our contracts limit how they may use the data. Our current list is at docs.klipspringer.net/legal/subprocessors
  • your Payment Processor, to connect your account and collect our fees;
  • your team members, who can see the names and roles of others on your account;
  • professional advisers, such as lawyers and accountants, who owe us duties of confidence;
  • legal authorities, when the law requires it, or when we need to protect the rights, safety, or property of anyone; and
  • a successor entity, if we are involved in a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets. We will tell you before your data becomes subject to a different privacy policy.

Your organization name and contact details appear on your public Event pages. You control what those pages show.

We do not sell personal information. We do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising.

items.title: 7. Cookies
items.text: We use only essential cookies. They keep you signed in and keep the Services secure. We do not use advertising or analytics cookies. Because these cookies are essential, the law does not require your consent for them.

items.title: 8. How long we keep organizer data
items.text:
• Account and team information: while your account is open. We delete it within 90 days after your account closes.
  • Billing records: for as long as tax and accounting law requires, which is generally 7 years.
  • Support communications and complaints: for 3 years after your last contact with us.
  • Reports and moderation records: for 3 years after the decision, so we can handle complaints and show compliance.
  • Logs: security and audit logs for up to 12 months, with IP addresses shortened.
  • Backups: overwritten within 90 days.

We may keep data longer if the law requires it, or if we need it to establish, exercise, or defend a legal claim.

items.title: 9. Security
items.text: We use reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect personal information. These include encryption in transit, access controls, multi-factor authentication for administrative access, and hashed password storage. No system is perfectly secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. If a breach affects your personal information, we will tell you as the law requires.

items.title: 10. Where we process organizer data
items.text: We are based in the United States, and we process organizer data there. If you are outside the United States, you give your information directly to us in the United States.

items.title: 11. Your rights
items.text:
Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:

  • access your personal information and get a copy;
  • correct it;
  • delete it;
  • receive it in a portable format;
  • object to, or ask us to restrict, certain processing;
  • withdraw consent, where we rely on consent; and
  • opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information.

To exercise a right, email privacy@klipspringer.net. We may need to verify your identity first. In some US states, an authorized agent may make a request for you. We respond within one month. If a request is complex, we may extend that time as the law allows, and we will tell you if we do.

We will not discriminate against you for exercising your rights.

If we deny your request, you may appeal by replying to our response. We will answer your appeal within the time the law requires. If we deny your appeal, you may contact your state attorney general.

If you are in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, you may also complain to your local data protection authority. In the UK, that is the Information Commissioner's Office. In Switzerland, it is the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner.

You may contact them instead of us about anything in this Policy.

items.title: 12. Children
items.text: The Services are for businesses and organizations. We do not knowingly collect organizer data from anyone under 18.

items.title: 13. Changes to this Policy
items.text: We may update this Policy. For material changes, we will tell you by email or by a message in the Services at least 30 days before the change takes effect. The effective date at the top shows when this Policy last changed.

items.title: 14. Contact
items.text: Questions about this Policy can go to privacy@klipspringer.net or to our postal address in section 1.
